Repeat steps 2-5 for each additional condition 7. click('Run') Workflow: search_knowledge_base Description: Use when you need to find information in the knowledge base by querying it 1. fill("Search", "<QUERY>") # e.g. "\"password to conference room A-561\"" 2. click("nth=0") Workflow: sort_list Description: Use when a ServiceNow list must be ordered by one or more fields. Preconditions: the target list is visible. Open the list builder, add one sort row per requested field, and set each row's direction. Outcome: the visible records are ordered by the configured sort levels. 1. click('.list_filter_toggle') 2. click('role=button') # add a sort row 3. select_option(<SORT_ROW>, <FIELD>) # e.g. 'nth=1', 'Assigned' 4. select_option(<SORT_ROW>, <DIRECTION>) # e.g. 'nth=1', 'ascending' 5. Repeat steps 2-4 for each additional sort level # e.g. 'Department', 'descending' 6. click('Run filter')
⬇ ### Skill 1. When using the global navigation filter to open an application, extract the exact application name from the task goal (e.g., 'Cost', 'Organization', 'Change') and fill it into the filter input. Do not guess or default to unrelated modules. Example: for goal 'Filter the organization list by Failed login attempts descending and First name descending.', after click('All'), the correct next action is fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', 'Organization') (not fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', 'User')). 2. After applying a list filter, always click the first record displayed in the filtered results list to proceed. Do not hallucinate record IDs or click records that do not appear in the current filtered view. Example: for goal 'Update change requests matching "#SERIES-d53387c5-c" in short description with planned start and end dates of 2026-10-23 18:03:56 to 2026-10-24 18:03:56 and 2026-10-24 18:04:56 to 2026-10-25 18:04:56.', after click("Run"), the correct next action is click('Preview record: CHG0047758') (not click('CHG0039945')). 3. During iterative multi-record updates, after saving one record, immediately click the preview card for the next record in the list to continue. Do not navigate back to the list view or home, as this breaks the workflow. Example: for goal 'Update change requests with short description containing #SERIES-2e0ff309-8 to set consecutive planned start and end dates...', after click('iframe[name="gsft_main"] >> internal:control=enter-frame >> #sysverb_update'), the correct next action is click('Preview record: CHG0047728') (not click('Back')). 4. When selecting a record immediately after applying a filter, extract the exact ID from the first visible result card and use it verbatim. Never guess, default to '0000000', or use prefixes not present in the UI. Example: for goal 'Delete all expense line items with short descriptions containing "#d8c6cc4a-8".', after click('Run'), the correct next action is click('Preview record: EXP-0c8e62eac-4') (not click('Preview record: EXP0000000')). 5. Immediately after clicking 'Run' to apply a filter, click the preview card of the first record in the resulting list. Extract the record ID exactly as displayed in the UI without modification or guessing. Example: for goal 'Delete all expense lines with short descriptions containing "#667f4906-3".', after click('Run'), the correct next action is click('Preview record: EXP-1a70c35fb-f') (not click('Preview record: EXP-1874474-4')). 6. During iterative updates, after saving a record, immediately click the preview card of the next record in the list. Do not attempt to interact with form fields or buttons on the saved record. Example: for goal 'Update change requests matching short description LIKE #SERIES-e0c27f06-5 to set planned start and end dates to 2029-06-09 17:43:16-2029-06-12 17:43:16 and 2029-06-12 17:44:16-2029-06-15 17:44:16.', after click('iframe[name="gsft_main"] >> internal:control=enter-frame >> #sysverb_update'), the correct next action is click('Preview record: CHG0040359') (not click('Planned start date | nt 7. Expense-related goals map to the 'Cost' application, not 'Expense'. Extract 'Cost' and fill it into the navigation filter. Example: for goal 'Delete all expense records with a short description containing SERIES-6283ff6a-0.', after click('All'), the correct next action is fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', 'Cost') (not fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', 'Expense')). 8. During iterative record deletion, after deleting a record, immediately click the preview card of the next record in the list. Do not click 'Yes' or attempt to finish the task until all records are processed. Example: for goal 'Delete all cost expense lines with short descriptions containing "#f219f65c-4".', after click('delete | nth=0'), the correct next action is click('Preview record: EXP-261dffc3c-d') (not click('Yes')). 9. When clicking a record immediately after applying a list filter, always read the actual record ID from the first visible result card in the table. Never construct, guess, or derive the record ID from the filter value or search term. Example: for goal 'Delete all expense records with short descriptions containing SERIES-d75a7d3a-f.', after click('Run'), the correct next action is click('Preview record: EXP-02665716761') (not click('Preview record: EXP-d75a7d3a-f')). ### Workflows Workflow: apply_filter_and_delete_matches Description: Filter a list by a specific field and value, then iterate through the results to open and delete each matching record. 1. click('All') # navigate to application menu 2. fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', 'Cost') # specify target application 3. click('All menu | role=button | Cost') # open application module 4. click('.list_filter_toggle') # enable filter row 5. select_option('nth=0', <FIELD>) # e.g., short_description 6. select_option('nth=0', <OPERATOR>) # e.g., LIKE 7. click('nth=0') # focus filter input 8. fill('nth=0', <VALUE>) # e.g., #SERIES-f258028d-7 9. click('Run') # execute filter 10. For each matching record <RECORD_ID>: - click('Preview record: <RECORD_ID>') - click('Open Record') - click('delete | nth=0') Workflow: apply_multi_field_or_filter Description: Use when records must be retrieved using a complex filter combining multiple fields with `OR` logic. Preconditions: The relevant list menu is accessible. Outcome: The list displays records matching at least one of the specified field/value pairs. 1. click('All') 2. fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', <MENU_NAME>) 3. click('All menu | role=button | <MENU_NAME>') 4. click('.list_filter_toggle') 5. select_option('nth=0', <FIELD_1>) 6. select_option('nth=0', <OPERATOR_1>) 7. click('nth=0') 8. fill('nth=0', <VALUE_1>) 9. click('nth=0') 10. click('.filterToolbar .filerTableAction:text-is("OR")') 11. select_option('nth=1', <FIELD_2>) 12. select_option('nth=1', <OPERATOR_2>) 13. click('.filterToolbar .filerTableAction:text-is("OR")') 14. select_option('nth=2', <FIELD_3>) 15. select_option('nth=2', <OPERATOR_3>) 16. click('nth=2') 17. fill('nth=2', <VALUE_3>) 18. click('Run') Workflow: assign_ticket_by_number Description: Use when a specific ticket must be located by its exact number and reassigned to a new user. Preconditions: The Service Desk list is visible. Outcome: The ticket's assigned user is updated and saved. 1. click('All') 2. fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', <MENU_NAME>) 3. click('All menu | role=button | <MENU_NAME>') 4. click('.list_filter_toggle') 5. click('nth=0') 6. select_option('nth=0', 'number') 7. select_option('nth=0', '=') 8. click('nth=0') 9. fill('nth=0', <TICKET_NUMBER>) 10. click('Run') 11. click('role=button | nth=0') 12. click('Open Record') 13. click('Assigned to | nth=0') 14. fill('Assigned to | nth=0', <ASSIGNEE_NAME>) 15. click('nth=0') 16. click('iframe[name="gsft_main"] >> internal:control=enter-frame >> #sysverb_update') Workflow: filter_and_update_schedule Description: When to filter a service list by specific criteria and sequentially update date fields for each resulting record. 1. click('All') # Navigate to the main module 2. fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', 'Change') # Specify the target application 3. click('All menu | role=button | Change') # Open the application module 4. click('.list_filter_toggle') # Open the filter builder 5. for each condition/field: select_option('nth=0', '<FIELD>') # e.g., short_description select_option('nth=0', '<OPERATOR>') # e.g., LIKE click('nth=0') # Focus the condition row fill('nth=0', '<VALUE>') # e.g., #SERIES-123456 6. click('Run') # Apply the filter to the list 7. for each record in filtered list: click('Preview record: <RECORD_ID>') # e.g., CHG0039945 click('Open Record') # Navigate to the detail form click('Planned start date | nth=0') # Select start date input fill('Planned start date | nth=0', '<START_DATE>') # e.g., 2028-12-30 11:23:45 click('Planned end date | nth=0') # Select end date input fill('Planned end date | nth=0', '<END_DATE>') # e.g., 2029-01-02 11:23:45 click('iframe[name="gsft_main"] >> internal:control=enter-frame >> #sysverb_update') # Save changes Workflow: apply_list_filter Description: Apply a single condition filter to a ServiceNow list to retrieve matching records. 1. click('All') # open global navigation menu 2. fill('All menu | placeholder="Filter"', <APP_NAME>) # e.g., Cost 3. click('All menu | role=button | <APP_NAME>') # e.g., Cost 4. click('.list_filter_toggle') # open filter UI 5. select_option('nth=0', <FIELD>) # e.g., short_description 6. select_option('nth=0', <OPERATOR>) # e.g., LIKE 7. click('nth=0') # focus filter row for input 8. fill('nth=0', <VALUE>) # e.g., #SERIES-f258028d-7 9. click('Run') # execute the filter
⬇ ### Skill 1. When a travel or booking form shows empty labeled fields or collapsed selectors, open the control before typing or choosing values; do not skip directly to filling hidden inputs. Example: for goal 'Find train options from New York, NY - Moynihan Train Hall (NYP) to Washington, DC - Union Station (WAS) for the 15th.', after no prior actions, the correct next action is click("From") (not fill("From", "New York, NY - Moynihan Train Hall (NYP)")). 2. On search/listing pages, satisfy explicit item-condition constraints before secondary perks like shipping, especially when the current results visibly violate the requested condition. Example: for goal 'Find new laptops priced between $400 and $500 with free shipping.', after fill("Search for anything", "new laptop") and click("Search"), the correct next action is click("New") (not click("Free shipping")). 3. Prefer stable navigation or mode controls over content shortcuts when the goal requires changing site context and the page offers a dedicated section/tab for that context. Example: for goal 'Browse museums in New York City.', after no prior actions, the correct next action is click("Cities") (not click("New York City")). 4. When a page shows broad department, section, or mode tabs alongside matching subitems, enter the parent container first before choosing a specific item or filter within it. Example: for goal 'Browse the Wine department with Kroger delivery available by 8:00pm.', after click(""), the correct next action is click("Departments") (not click("Wine")). 5. Prefer click on visible tabs, chips, or pseudo-checkbox labels to activate a filter when the control is presented as a clickable text/value element rather than a standard checkbox input. Example: for goal 'View the Coupons & Deals section filtered to LTO offers.', after click("Coupons & Deals"), the correct next action is click("LTO") (not set_checked("LTO", "true")). 6. When the goal combines a search target with a specific search mode or product type, choose the mode tab that matches the requested service before opening broader category pages or destination-specific shortcuts. Example: for goal 'Book hourly parking at Atlanta International Airport on Spine Road in College Park, Georgia.', after no prior actions, the correct next action is click("Hourly") (not click("Airport")). 7. When the goal names a specific entity but the landing page only shows broad site sections or a search box, start with the site's search control instead of a top-level category or guessed result. Example: for goal 'Save Atlantis to a collection.', after no prior actions, the correct next action is fill("Search", "Atlantis") (not click("Atlantis")). 8. When a date or text field is visibly an input or picker trigger, click it to open/focus the control before typing or selecting a value; do not type into unopened widgets or use select_option on non-dropdown toggles. Example: for goal 'Find hotel options for 1 room for 2 adults and 1 child age 0, staying from the 24th to the 27th, with price range and area filters applied.', after click("hotels."), the correct next action is click("checkin") (not fill("Check In", "24")). 9. After selecting an item in a date-filtered planner, if a visible current date chip/value is shown next to a date picker, click that existing date value to open or change the date instead of typing a new date into the picker label. Example: for goal 'View the planned service changes for Route 4 on Wednesday, May 3, 2023.', after click(""), click("Planned Service Changes"), fill("Search Routes", "4"), and click("4"), the correct next action is click("04/12/2023") (not fill("Select Date", "05/03/2023")). ### Workflows Workflow: complete_contact_or_request_form Description: Use when a site presents a lead, inquiry, rental, demo-drive, or checkout-gating form that asks for personal/contact details before continuing. Preconditions: the relevant form is already open. Outcome: required identity/contact fields are filled and the form is submitted or advanced. 1. fill(<NAME_OR_CONTACT_FIELD>, <VALUE>) # e.g. "First Name", "lastName", "Email Address *", "phone", "zip" 2. fill(<ADDITIONAL_REQUIRED_FIELD>, <VALUE>) # e.g. address, city, employer, member number, market, message 3. select_option(<OPTION_FIELD>, <OPTION>) # if present; e.g. state, market 4. click(<SUBMIT_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Submit", "Submit and Continue", "Sign Up", "Proceed to checkout", "Send Email" Workflow: search_location_then_choose_suggestion Description: Use when a site requires typing a place, venue, airport, park, city, destination, or station and then selecting one autocomplete suggestion before proceeding. Preconditions: a searchable location input is visible. Outcome: the intended location is selected into the form or search flow. 1. fill(<LOCATION_FIELD>, <QUERY>) # e.g. "City or airport", "Where are you going?", "Select a park", "Departure station..." 2. click(<SUGGESTED_LOCATION>) # e.g. "SFO - San Francisco International, CA", "Alagnak Wild River", "Los Angeles, CA, USA" Workflow: navigate_to_section_then_open_subpage Description: Use when you need to reach a topic/category section and then open a related destination within it. 1. click("<SECTION>") # example: "Music", "News", "Fantasy", "NFL", "Watchlist 5" 2. click("<DESTINATION>") # example: "Follow", "View All", "Download the App .", "Edit", "VIDEOS", "What to Watch" Workflow: configure_travel_party Description: Use when a booking flow asks for traveler or guest counts, room counts, or passenger composition before search. Preconditions: the occupancy/traveler selector is open or accessible. Outcome: the party composition is set. 1. click(<PARTY_CONTROL>) # e.g. "1 traveler", "1 room, 2 guests", "Number of Guests" 2. click(<INCREMENT_OR_ADD_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Increase adults", "Add Adults", "Add Rooms" 3. select_option(<AGE_OR_COUNT_FIELD>, <OPTION>) # if present; e.g. child age, total passengers 4. click(<DONE_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Done", "Confirm" Workflow: search_after_form_setup Description: Use when a site requires entering search criteria and then explicitly launching results. Preconditions: required search inputs have been populated. Outcome: the site navigates to a results page. 1. fill(<SEARCH_FIELD>, <QUERY>) # e.g. "Search", "Search Site", "Search for anything", "Airport" 2. click(<SEARCH_TRIGGER>) # e.g. "Search", "Find", "Submit Search", "Get cheapest tickets" Workflow: browse_category_hierarchy Description: Use when reaching the target content requires drilling down through two or more navigation levels such as department -> subcategory -> sub-subcategory. Preconditions: top-level navigation is accessible. Outcome: the agent lands on a focused listing or section. 1. click(<TOP_LEVEL_CATEGORY>) # e.g. "WOMEN", "Sports", "Movies", "Shop" 2. click(<SUBCATEGORY>) # e.g. "Cropped Tops", "NFL", "In Theaters", "Vitamin C" 3. click(<DEEPER_CATEGORY_OR_SECTION>) # e.g. "All NFL Tickets", "Coming Soon", "Shirts and Hoodies" Workflow: apply_filters_to_results Description: Use when a results or listing page offers one or more facet filters such as size, color, amenities, genre, stock, cancellation, stops, or accessibility. Preconditions: a results page or filter panel is open. Outcome: results are narrowed to match requested constraints. 1. click(<FILTER_GROUP>) # e.g. "Genre", "Color", "Amenities", "Filter", "Size" 2. click(<FILTER_OPTION>) # e.g. "comedy", "BLACK", "Business center (11)", "wheelchair" 3. click(<APPLY_OR_SHOW_RESULTS_CONTROL>) # if present; e.g. "Apply", "Show 10 Results", "Done" Workflow: sort_results Description: Use when a listing page supports changing result order after search or filtering. Preconditions: sortable results are visible. Outcome: results are reordered by the chosen criterion. 1. click(<SORT_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Sort by", "Featured undefined", "Sort by Relevance" 2. click(<SORT_OPTION>) # or select_option when implemented as a dropdown; e.g. "Price (lowest first)", "Best Sellers undefined" 3. select_option(<SORT_DROPDOWN>, <OPTION>) # e.g. "Price - Lowest", "Highest Price", "Lowest mileage first" Workflow: open_item_from_results Description: Use when the goal is to inspect a specific product, hotel, vehicle, article, game, or media item after search/browse/filtering. Preconditions: a results list is visible. Outcome: the chosen item's detail page or modal is opened. 1. click(<ITEM_RESULT>) # e.g. "Waking Up: A Guide to Spirituality Without Religion", "Nice Hostel Kameari", "View Details" 2. click(<DETAILS_OR_CONTINUE_CONTROL>) # if needed; e.g. "See Details", "View Page", "See availability" Workflow: add_item_to_cart_or_bag Description: Use when purchasing or collecting a product/add-on requires opening an item and adding it to the cart, bag, or basket. Preconditions: the desired item page or listing action is visible. Outcome: the item is added to the shopping cart/bag. 1. click(<ITEM>) # e.g. product title, ticket add-on, meal deal 2. click(<ADD_TO_CART_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Add to cart", "Add To Cart", "Add to Bag", "Add ... to Basket" 3. click(<POST_ADD_CONTINUE_CONTROL>) # if present; e.g. "No Thanks", "Checkout Now", "View cart" Workflow: choose_variant_then_add_to_cart Description: Use when an item must be configured with a size, quantity, or similar variant before adding it to cart. Preconditions: the item detail page is open. Outcome: the selected variant is added to the cart. 1. click(<VARIANT_GROUP>) # e.g. "Size", quantity selector, ticket quantity 2. click(<VARIANT_OPTION>) # e.g. "L", "9", "3", "$107 /ea" 3. click(<ADD_TO_CART_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Add to cart", "Add to Bag" Workflow: save_item_to_list_or_wishlist Description: Use when the goal is to save one or more items to a named list, collection, or wishlist rather than purchase immediately. Preconditions: save/list controls are available. Outcome: the item is stored in the chosen list. 1. click(<SAVE_OR_LIST_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Create a list", "Add To Collection", "Add to Wish List" 2. fill(<LIST_NAME_FIELD>, <LIST_NAME>) # if creating a new list; e.g. "Add a title (Required)", "Name" 3. click(<CONFIRM_SAVE_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Create", "Save", "Done", "Save to <LIST>" Workflow: select_dropdown_options_then_continue Description: Use when a form or finder is primarily driven by dropdown selections such as year/make/model, make/model, season, state, or fare/class preferences. Preconditions: the relevant select controls are visible. Outcome: the configured options are applied and the flow advances. 1. select_option(<SELECT_FIELD>, <OPTION>) # e.g. "Year" -> "2006", "Make" -> "Honda", "State" -> "Colorado" 2. select_option(<NEXT_SELECT_FIELD>, <OPTION>) # e.g. "Model" -> "Civic", season, sort order 3. click(<CONTINUE_OR_SEARCH_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Next", "Search", "See Cars for Sale" Workflow: request_booking_or_reservation Description: Use when, after narrowing results, the site requires a booking/reservation action to proceed to purchase or availability confirmation. Preconditions: a specific result or offering is visible. Outcome: the reservation/booking flow is initiated. 1. click(<RESULT_ACTION>) # e.g. "See availability", "View Rates", "Check Availability" 2. click(<BOOK_OR_RESERVE_CONTROL>) # e.g. "Reserve", "Book Now", "Reserve with Genius discount" 3. click(<FINAL_CONFIRM_CONTROL>) # if present; e.g. "submit", "SELECT" Workflow: navigate_to_information_section Description: Use when the task is informational and requires opening a specific tab, subsection, or article within a site after reaching the relevant entity or category. Preconditions: the parent page or section is open. Outcome: the requested informational content is displayed. 1. click(<PARENT_SECTION>) # e.g. "Stats", "Community", "Find a Park by State", "Support" 2. click(<TARGET_SUBSECTION>) # e.g. "Season Leaders", "Popular Photos", "Basic Information", "Find My AirPods" 3. click(<REFINEMENT_OR_DATE_CONTROL>) # if present; e.g. "Next day", "April", "Mar 26" Workflow: search_then_refine_then_select Description: Use when a task starts with a keyword search, then applies one or more refinements, then opens a final result. Preconditions: a site search box is available. Outcome: a narrowed result is selected. 1. fill(<SEARCH_FIELD>, <QUERY>) # e.g. "Search Amazon", "Search Site", "Search for anything" 2. click(<SEARCH_TRIGGER_OR_SUGGESTION>) # e.g. "Search", autocomplete suggestion 3. click(<FILTER_OR_SORT_OPTION>) # e.g. "Paperback", "4 Stars & Up", "Price + Shipping: highest first" 4. click(<FINAL_RESULT>) # e.g. book title, product title, event result Workflow: navigate_to_category Description: Use this to open a broad shopping/listing area and then choose a specific category, tab, or subsection. 1. click("<TOP_LEVEL_SECTION>") # example: "Deals", "Shopping Cart", "Today's Deals", "Coupons & Deals", site/home link 2. click("<CATEGORY_OR_SUBSECTION>") # example: "DISH Outdoors", "Trending (2)", "LTO", "Inventory", "Shows By Date", "Remove"

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
